title: Q3 Strategy: Capacity SLOs + Predictive Autoscale for Dedicated Pools
creator: Sofia Malik
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated customers increasingly request predictable latency and cost guarantees when using reserved GPU pools. Current autoscale behavior is reactive and tuned for cost efficiency, which leads to measurable tail-latency regressions under bursty workloads. This initiative defines a Q3 roadmap to introduce capacity-level SLOs and a predictive autoscale layer that reduces SLO breaches and improves economic predictability for customers.

Scope:
- Define capacity SLOs (p50/p95/p99 generation latency, queue length thresholds, cold-start incidence) at the Dedicated pool level.
- Implement a predictive autoscaler that leverages short-term traffic forecasting, workload-class signals (latency-sensitive vs best-effort), and pre-warming heuristics.
- Add console controls to let customers set SLO targets and autoscale aggressiveness per pool.
- Instrument end-to-end observability (SLO dashboards, alerting, and post-incident analysis).

Out-of-scope (this quarter): model runtime kernel changes and lower-level quantization improvements — those remain on the runtime roadmap but will be coordinated as dependencies.
objectives: Establish formal capacity SLO definitions for Dedicated pools
Ship a predictive autoscale prototype that reduces P99 latency breaches by >=50% on target workloads
Expose SLO controls in the Console for customer configuration
Create SLO-based alerting and weekly health dashboard for capacity owners
success_metrics: P99 generation latency breaches reduced by >=50% in Canary customers
Mean queue wait time reduced by >=40% during burst windows
Customers using SLO controls increase Dedicated pool utilization predictability (measured via variance of provisioned vs needed capacity) by >=30%
Number of incidents caused by autoscale lag reduced quarter-over-quarter
milestones: 2026-03-31: SLO definitions and customer configuration UX draft complete
2026-04-21: Predictive autoscale v0 prototype (simulation + unit tests)
2026-05-12: Canary deployment to 2 strategic customers and internal workloads
2026-05-30: SLO dashboard GA in Console (read-only) for canaries
2026-06-15: Post-canary review and go/no-go for broader rollout
risks: Predictive model misforecasting causing overprovisioning and increased cost
Tight coupling between autoscaler and runtime kernel assumptions leading to unforeseen regressions
Complexity of exposing SLOs could confuse customers if defaults are not sensible
Instrumenting accurate metrics (end-to-end) may require infra changes that slip the timeline
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal + synthetic workload validation
Phase B: Two canary customers (staggered 2-week ramps)
Phase C: Gradual opt-in across Dedicated customers with telemetry gating
Phase D: Auto-enablement for low-risk pools with conservative defaults (post-qa)
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions documented and reviewed with SRE and Customer Success
Predictive autoscaler prototype runs in sandbox and shows >30% reduction in simulated P99 breaches
Console UI exposes SLO target and autoscale aggressiveness with validation rules
SLO dashboard reflects real-time and historical metrics for canary pools
Runbook and rollback plan created for canary and broader rollout
